title: TP stability: dashboards + alerting for collectives/scheduler health (oncall-usable)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Goal
Create an oncall-usable dashboard + alert set for TP hangs/timeouts that helps quickly distinguish:
- comm/collective stall (e.g., NCCL async error not surfaced, ring stuck)
- kernel stall (no forward progress but comms look normal)
- scheduler starvation / barrier deadlock (queue builds, group not making step progress)

This workstream is the glue between new runtime signals (ENG-2404) + watchdog/quarantine behavior (ENG-2407) and SRE paging.

Scope
1) Dashboards (Grafana)
- A “TP Collectives & Scheduler Health” dashboard with panels that work at:
  - fleet view (Hosted pool / Dedicated cluster)
  - node view (per host)
  - TP-group view (per model/route + tp_group_id)

2) Alerts
- Define alert rules + thresholds with clear runbook actions and low noise.
- Alerts must page SRE only when action is required; otherwise route to Slack channel for investigation.

3) Oncall usability validation
- Dry-run with SRE oncall (Tomáš + Jacob) using real incident artifacts (Feb 13 Sev1) and at least one staging repro.

Dashboards: required panels (v1)
A. SLO/impact correlation
- Request timeouts rate (by route/model) vs 5xx rate
- Active streams count + stream duration distribution (p50/p95/p99)
- Dedicated: per-cluster error budget burn (if available) annotated with runtime rollouts

B. TP-group health (scheduler-level)
- TP groups by state: healthy | suspect | quarantined | resetting (ENG-2407)
- Quarantine events count + resets count (rate + cumulative)
- Scheduling backlog depth / queue time (per route/model and per host)
- “No forward progress” duration (derived from per-rank progress counters / last_step_timestamp)

C. Collectives (comm-level)
- Collective latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) by op type (all_reduce, all_gather, reduce_scatter)
- Collective timeout count (by op type, by tp_group_id)
- NCCL async error detections count (by error code if available)
- Collective in-flight count (helps see if we’re stuck on a single long collective)

D. Kernel/compute stall indicators
- Tokens/sec (per route/model) and sudden drops
- GPU SM utilization + mem utilization (at node level)
- “Kernel step time” p99 (where instrumented)
- CUDA error counters / Xid counts (if available via node exporter; otherwise link-out)

E. Drill-down tables
- Top TP groups by collective p99
- Top TP groups by watchdog triggers in last 1h
- Top nodes by resets in last 24h

Alerts: proposed rules (v1)
Note: exact metric names depend on ENG-2404/2407 implementation. Where unknown, use placeholders and align before merge.

Paging (SRE) — action required
1) TP group quarantine storm
- Condition: quarantines_rate > 3 / 5m for a pool/cluster OR quarantined_groups > 2% of active_groups for 10m
- Why: likely systemic stall; needs traffic shift / rollback / capacity mitigation
- Runbook: shift traffic away from affected pool; consider disabling TP for impacted route; evaluate rollback; check NCCL error signals

2) Collective timeout spike with customer impact
- Condition: collective_timeouts_rate > N / 5m AND (timeouts_rate or 5xx_rate above baseline) for 10m
- Why: typically correlates with hanging groups
- Runbook: confirm comm stall signature; quarantine should self-heal but spike implies systemic issue; consider draining nodes

3) “No forward progress” without recovery
- Condition: suspect_groups > 0 for > 10m OR max_no_progress_seconds > 300 with stable load
- Why: watchdog not recovering or false negative
- Runbook: verify watchdog firing; if not firing, treat as bug/regression; mitigate by draining hosts / restarting workers

Non-paging (Slack #eng-runtime + ticket)
4) Elevated collective p99 without errors
- Condition: collective_p99_ms > baseline*2 for 30m; no timeouts
- Why: perf regression, not necessarily incident

5) Reset rate above normal but no customer impact
- Condition: tp_group_resets_rate > baseline*X for 1h, but no timeout/5xx correlation
- Why: possible false positives in watchdog tuning; collect evidence

Alert quality requirements
- Must include links: dashboard + relevant runbook section + “how to silence” guidance.
- Must include labels: pool/cluster, route/model, runtime version.
- Must have an explicit owner rotation (SRE primary; runtime secondary).

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard exists with fleet/node/TP-group drill-down and is used in at least one oncall shadow or staging repro.
- Alert rules merged in observability-pack with documented thresholds and rationale.
- Noise check: no more than 1 false-positive page/day in canary pools (first week). If exceeded, adjust thresholds.
- Runbook sections updated to reference new panels/alerts.

Open questions
- What is the canonical “per-rank progress” metric name + cardinality control strategy? Need to ensure we don’t explode series count (cap to active TP groups only; sample; or export per-group aggregate + optional per-rank debug).
- How do we tag tp_group_id in a way that’s stable for a single hang investigation but not long-lived high-cardinality?
- Dedicated environments: do we ship the same dashboards/alerts to customer-managed Grafana, or Redwood-managed only? (PM/CS guidance needed.)
comments: 2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Creating as P1 for oncall readiness. We can’t ship watchdog/quarantine without a clear dashboard + paging policy; Feb 13 Sev1 highlighted we didn’t know comm stall vs kernel stall quickly enough.

2025-02-20 (Sergio Costa): Started draft dashboard JSON based on existing runtime overview. Need final metric names from ENG-2404 instrumentation PR; for now building layout + templating (pool, cluster, model, route, host).

2025-02-22 (Allison Grant): Please avoid per-rank series in default dashboard. Prefer per-tp-group aggregates + a separate ‘debug’ dashboard gated behind a variable. Also ensure every alert has a runbook link and a clear owner label.

2025-02-26 (Aisha Bello): Proposed baseline thresholds from Hosted us-east high-load pool: collective p99 typically 8–20ms; timeouts are near zero. Suggest alert on relative delta + correlation to request timeouts rather than absolute p99 alone.

2025-03-01 (Tomáš Novák): Oncall review request: want a single panel that answers ‘are we stuck and where’ in <60s. Suggest top table: (tp_group_id, state, no_progress_s, collective_inflight, last_nccl_err, route/model).

2025-03-05 (Sergio Costa): PR in observability-pack updated (PR-502) with initial dashboard + 3 alert rules in non-paging mode. Blocking on ENG-2407 final metric names for quarantine/reset counters before enabling paging.
